settings.editor: Top Notch Painting is a division of Top Notch Logworks, which has built log and timber homes and resorts here since 1999. We know what it takes to make a log finish last.

background_image.alt: Stained log home with a wraparound deck

settings.editor:
If you want your home to look its best and get the longest life from a finish, everything depends on how the logs are prepared before any stain goes on. Skipping prep cuts the life of a finish short, and you end up paying to refinish sooner.

Colorado's dry climate doesn't protect logs. Intense UV breaks down finishes and wood, letting moisture in. We use products from Sashco and Perma-Chink, made specifically for log and timber homes, and we're trained and certified to apply them.

• Media blasting to remove old, failing finishes
  • Chemical cleaning and brightening
  • Sanding and stripping where needed
  • Color samples on your own logs before you choose
  • Preservatives, stains and topcoats from Sashco and Perma-Chink
Old, failing finishes stripped back to clean wood so new stain can soak in.
Graying and mildew removed so the wood's natural color comes back.
Preservative, stain and topcoat applied to the manufacturer's specifications.
Gaps and checks sealed against drafts, moisture and pests.
Damaged log ends and beams cut out, replaced and treated.
Regular touch-up coats that keep a finish strong, so small jobs stay small.
We look at the whole home: finish condition, checks, chinking and any signs of rot.
Windows, doors, roofs and landscaping are masked and covered before blasting or staining.
Media blasting, cleaning, brightening and sanding take the logs back to clean wood.
Preservative, stain and topcoat applied to the manufacturer's specifications.
We tell you honestly when the next maintenance coat is due.

settings.html:
How often should a log home be restained?
It depends on sun exposure and the product used. South- and west-facing walls need attention first. Regular maintenance coats extend the life of a finish and cost far less than a full restoration.
Why do you media blast?
A new finish only lasts if it bonds to clean wood. Blasting removes old, failing stain and weathered wood fibers without soaking the logs, so the new finish soaks in properly.
Can you match our current color?
Yes. We apply samples on your own logs so you can see the color in place before you choose.
Do you check on the home after the work is done?
Yes. We'll tell you when maintenance is due, and we're happy to come back and look at the home so small problems never become big ones.
